turns.user: how do I do a deadlift
turns.reply:
Here are the key cues to focus on:

1. Set your stance — feet hip-width apart, with the bar sitting directly over the middle of your foot.
2. Brace before you lift — take a deep breath into your belly, wedge your hips down, and pull the slack out of the bar until it feels heavy in your hands.
3. Push the floor away — drive through your mid-foot to stand up, keeping the bar close to your shins the whole way up.

That's the core of it — keeping the bar over your mid-foot is what protects your lower back.

turns.reply:
Here is the complete step-by-step breakdown:

1. Setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, shins about an inch from the bar, with the bar directly over your mid-foot.
2. Grip: Hinge at your hips, bend your knees slightly, and grip the bar just outside your legs with double-overhand or mixed grip.
3. Lat engagement: Think about squeezing a orange under each armpit to turn your upper back on and lock your spine in place.
4. The wedge: Pull your chest up, drop your hips into position, and take the slack out of the bar until you hear a click.
5. The pull: Push the floor away with your legs rather than pulling with your lower back, keeping the bar touching your legs all the way up.
6. Lockout: Stand tall by squeezing your glutes at the top — don't lean back or hyperextend your lower back.
7. Lowering: Hinge at the hips first to send the bar straight down past your knees, then bend at the knees to set it on the floor.

Focusing on pushing the floor away turns it into a leg and hip movement, which keeps your back completely safe.
